questions.answer: Off campus

questions.answer: With the help from tafl it was quite easy

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
That you will appreciate living in walking distance to the university, so I will recommend that.
Also that there isn't apartments with more than 3 bedrooms.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Im not sure what is ment here, but they helped us with everything from student ID card to the visa registartion.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I think all kind if help was available. The staff on Tafl were always helpfull with everything from concerns to tech-problems.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The classes were chosen beforehand but I was satisfied with the classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Im still not sure what the registration part means, but overall everything about the stay went without major problems and both Ku and Tafl can help with what might be difficult or confusing.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The levels fitted well with our level, but we were still challenged in a good way. There were a lot of homework that were difficult to keep up with, but overall the levels of the courses were great.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The stile of teaching was similar with the one I Denmark because of the very small amount of students in the class, but in Egypt the classes were in arabic only. There were also two professors in each cours, which is different from ucph.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: These were all great and useful

questions.answer: Cooking club, singing club, cinema club and calligraphy club

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Cooking club. It was cozy and you got to taste Egyptian food.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Kairo, Fayoum, Siwa or the beach at the greek club in Alexandria

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: For me it was difficult because of how different it is from everything im used to, but everyone is very hospitable.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: How everyone stares at you in the streets, and how men will catcall you on the streets as well.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How everyone is friendly and hospitable

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared for the big amount of homework, but also know that your language will indeed improve!
The staff at tafl is very kind, understanding and helpful with everything.
Talk with the students from other nationalities. It is nice with a little community at tafl.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
You can pretty much live off of your SU depending on how many trips in the weekends you wish to take.
As a woman, be prepared for the amount of attention specifically from men that you will receive on the streets, but also know that they aren't unfriendly.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Understanding the culture in a way a textbook wouldn't teach me. Also to feel my arabic language improve and being able to speak with the locals.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
The greatest challenge might be how chaotic and noisy Egypt is, so it was difficult to fully relax during the stay.
The amount of homework was also challenging because we wanted to finish them all and do it thoroughly.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Overall a very great and educational experience that I wouldn't be without.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
